title: Nepal helps Bhutan strengthen quake preparedness with support from PM Modi-backed coalition - The Hindu
description: Nepal helps Bhutan strengthen quake preparedness with support from PM Modi-backed coalition  The Hindu
publisher.title: The Hindu
full_article:
A full-scale earthquake simulation in Bhutan's capital has exposed gaps in emergency equipment and resource mobilisation while testing how authorities, hospitals and emergency responders would coordinate after a major quake, with Nepal's earthquake experts providing technical support for the exercise.

The simulation recreated a scenario akin to a magnitude 7.5 earthquake in Thimphu, which involved mass casualties, damaged buildings, disrupted roads and power supply, and tested how authorities would make decisions, communicate, coordinate rescue operations and mobilise resources in the aftermath of such a disaster.

The National Society for Earthquake Technology-Nepal (NSET), with support from the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) and Bhutanese authorities, designed and facilitated the full-scale simulation exercise on June 23 as part of efforts to strengthen the Thimphu Earthquake Contingency Plan. Findings of the exercise were published by a Nepali weekly on Saturday (August 15, 2026).

CDRI was conceptualised by India and launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the United Nations Climate Action Summit in New York in 2019 to promote the resilience of infrastructure systems to climate and disaster risks.

It has more than 50 member countries, which include India, Nepal, Bhutan, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Germany, Italy, the U.S., the U.K., Sri Lanka and the Netherlands. It also brings together bodies like the World Bank, Asian Development Bank, United Nations Development Programme and European Union.

The exercise in Thumpu followed a tabletop simulation and aimed to test the contingency arrangements in a field setting, according to state-run Bhutan Broadcasting Service (BBS) and the Nepali Times weekly newspaper.

Bhutan and Nepal lie in the seismically active Himalayan region and are vulnerable to major earthquakes. Bhutan was hit by a magnitude 5.5 earthquake on June 7, while a magnitude 5 earthquake struck Rukum East in western Nepal on July 19.

Bhutan's deadliest recorded earthquake was an estimated magnitude 8.5 quake in 1714. In Nepal, more than 9,000 people were killed when a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck in April 2015, followed by powerful aftershocks, including a magnitude 7.3 quake the following month.

During the full-scale exercise, Bhutanese authorities created a mass-casualty scenario involving the country’s largest referral hospital and two primary healthcare centres, Nepali Times reported.

The scenario assumed that some emergency medical staff could not reach the hospital because of family emergencies or blocked roads, while the hospitals themselves were without power.

BBS reported that the exercise involved response operations at nine locations in Thimphu, including a simulated hotel collapse, severely damaged residential buildings and a fire in Olakha — a prominent urban area and commercial zone in the capital city.

At the hospital, patients and staff were evacuated to designated safe zones, temporary medical tents were set up and ambulances transported simulated casualties from affected areas, BBS reported.

The exercise also highlighted gaps in the availability of equipment and resources that could be mobilised quickly to establish field hospitals if the main hospital were compromised.

“Currently, through this simulation exercise, we realised that we don’t have that kind of resource to be mobilised immediately and set up field hospitals,” BBS quoted Phub Tshering, incident commander of the earthquake simulation exercise at the hospital, as saying.

The exercise also tested multi-agency coordination, communication, decision-making and resource mobilisation.

CDRI Director General Amit Prothi told the press that simulations were important because, unlike in a real disaster, participants knew in advance where resources would be needed and could therefore identify weaknesses in their systems.

The simulation team also assessed critical infrastructure, including 11 bridges, a hospital, an electricity terminal, the telecom network and a food supply warehouse, Nepali Times reported.

The four-hour exercise involved around 500 people in various roles and was attended by Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay, who is the country's overall disaster response commander, the newspaper said.

The outcome of the exercise was analysed, and NSET prepared a series of recommendations to strengthen Bhutan's earthquake preparedness.

One recommendation was for Bhutan to establish at least one six-member earthquake first-responder rescue squad for every ward serving 15,000-20,000 people, according to Nepali Times.

Surya Narayan Shrestha of NSET told Nepali Times that Prime Minister Tobgay said Bhutan needed to learn from Nepal due to the similarity in their circumstances.

The exercise was part of a broader effort to strengthen Bhutan's preparedness for a major earthquake, especially for urban centres like Thimpu.

title: NRN Urges Nepal Govt to Establish Shelter Houses for Migrant Workers - Ratopati
description: NRN Urges Nepal Govt to Establish Shelter Houses for Migrant Workers  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
China. The Non-Resident Nepali Association (NRNA) has urged the Nepal government to establish 'Shelter Houses' for the rescue and immediate accommodation of Nepali workers facing problems in countries with a large number of Nepali migrant workers.

During the session on 'Safe Foreign Employment and Reintegration' held as part of the NRNA Asia-Pacific Regional Conference, which began in Guangzhou, China on Saturday, participants stated that rescuing and assisting workers becomes difficult when there is no provision for their safe shelter during times of trouble.

NRNA Vice President and program chairperson Khagendra Neupane stated that the government itself should establish 'Shelter Houses' in countries with a large number of Nepali workers.

He mentioned that when workers face problems, NRNA representatives have to manage the situation on their own initiative due to the lack of immediate safe places to keep them. Neupane added that in some cases, NRNA representatives themselves face legal issues and even imprisonment while trying to accommodate troubled workers.

He drew the government's attention to the fact that despite their demand for 'Shelter Houses' for years, the government has not paid heed.

Neupane also emphasized the need to send Nepali workers for foreign employment only after providing them with skills training. For this, he suggested establishing 'Skill Academies' and skill testing centers in collaboration between the government and NRNA.

He stated that although NRNA representatives provide immediate assistance to Nepali workers facing problems abroad, issues arise due to the lack of formal legal recognition. He also urged the government to recognize NRNA representatives as 'Honorary' or unpaid labor envoys.

'NRNA is working like an Ambassador'

Member of Parliament and former Minister of Communications, Jagdish Kharel, said that NRNS abroad are working like ambassadors to solve the problems of Nepalis.

He pledged to advocate with the government on necessary matters, stating that although the position of an unpaid envoy may seem minor, it can play a significant role in resolving the problems of Nepali workers.

'NRNs abroad are working like ambassadors. Although the position of an unpaid envoy may seem minor, its role is significant. I am committed to advocating with the government on necessary matters,' Kharel said.

Kharel mentioned that the government and the Rastriya Swatantra Party are closely understanding the problems of Nepalis living abroad and will work towards their solutions. He also stated that collaboration among all parties is necessary for the skill development of workers going for foreign employment.

The Situation of Sending Unskilled Workers Must End

Member of Parliament Ain Mahar stated that foreign employment must be made systematic, safe, and dignified. He emphasized that special attention should be paid to skill development to end the situation where Nepal is known only as a country sending unskilled workers.

'Foreign employment must be made systematic and dignified. Work must be done on skill development. Nepal must rise above the situation of being known only as a country sending unskilled workers,' Mahar said.

'After Embassies, Nepalis Remember NRNA'

Krishu Chhetri, Deputy Chief of the Diaspora Coordination Division at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said that after Nepali embassies and missions abroad, Nepalis remember NRNA.

He praised NRNA's role, stating that even without formal government recognition, NRNA representatives are practically working as labor envoys.

'After Nepali embassies and missions abroad, Nepalis remember NRNA. Even without formal government recognition, NRNS are working as labor envoys. This role is commendable,' Chhetri said.

Separate Conference on Foreign Employment to be Held in Nepal

NRNA President Dr. Hemraj Sharma stated that more work needs to be done in the field of foreign employment, and therefore, a broader discussion on this topic is necessary. He informed that a separate, large-scale conference on foreign employment will be organized in Nepal within a few months.

'More work needs to be done in the field of foreign employment. As a broad discussion is necessary on this topic, we will organize a separate conference in Nepal within a few months,' Sharma said.

He mentioned that NRNA is doing a lot of work in the field of foreign employment and will conduct more programs in the future.

Mental Health Issues in Foreign Employment Also Raised

NRNA Vice President Junu Gurung provided information about the work being done regarding the mental health of Nepalis in foreign employment and the programs to be conducted in the future.

She stated that more programs are needed to identify and address mental health issues seen during foreign employment.

The conference has urged the government to establish training centers and skill testing centers to teach skills for sending not only unskilled workers but also skilled manpower in foreign employment.

Participants stated that collaboration between the government, private sector, and NRNA is necessary to produce skilled manpower and manage their deployment in foreign employment.

Demand for Legal Rights

NRNA representatives from various countries stated that although they provide immediate rescue, legal, and other assistance to Nepalis in trouble, problems arise due to the lack of formal legal authority.

Although NRNA has been drawing the attention of the Nepal government to recognize its representatives as unpaid labor envoys, this issue was raised again at the conference as it has not been implemented.

During the program, thematic presentations were made on the condition of Nepali workers in various countries, the problems they face, and solutions.

Deepak Pun presented on the condition of Nepali workers in South Korea, Eknath Khatiwada in Laos, Khagaraj Gautam in Japan, Tillochan Gautam in Malaysia, and Yuvraj Neupane in Macau. Journalist Anil Adhikari also presented on the problems and solutions for workers.

NRNA Chief Executive Officer Rajendra Kumar Raut provided information about the work being done by the organization in the field of foreign employment and labor.

The program was conducted by Yagyaraj Subedi, and journalist Uddhav Bhattarai took notes for the keynote.

NRNA has announced that it will organize a separate, large-scale conference on foreign employment in Nepal after some time. NRNA stated that the conference will further discuss issues such as safe foreign employment, skill development, labor rights, rescue, and reintegration among the government, concerned bodies, and expatriate Nepalis.

चीन। अनिवासी नेपाली संघ नेपाल सरकारसँ पैघ संख्यामे नेपाली प्रवासी श्रमिकसभ रहल देशमे समस्याक सामना करयवला नेपाली श्रमिकसभके उद्धार आ तत्काल आवासके लेल ‘आश्रय गृह’ स्थापित करबाक आग्रह केने अछि ।

चीन केरऽ ग्वांगझू म॑ शनिदिन शुरू होलऽ एनआरएनए एशिया-प्रशांत क्षेत्रीय सम्मेलन के हिस्सा के रूप म॑ आयोजित ‘सुरक्षित विदेशी रोजगार आरू पुनर्वास’ के सत्र के दौरान प्रतिभागी सिनी न॑ कहलकै कि मजदूरऽ क॑ बचाना आरू सहायता करना मुश्किल होय जाय छै जब॑ परेशानी के समय म॑ ओकरऽ सुरक्षित आश्रय के प्रावधान नै होय छै ।

एनआरएनए के उपाध्यक्ष आ कार्यक्रम अध्यक्ष खगेन्द्र न्यौपाने नेपाली श्रमिकक पैघ संख्या वाला देश मे सरकार स्वयं ‘आश्रय गृह’ स्थापित करबाक बात कहलनि ।

ओ उल्लेख केलथि जे जखन मजदूर कए समस्या क सामना करय पड़ैत अछि त ओकरा रखबा लेल तत्काल सुरक्षित स्थान क अभाव मे एनआरएनए प्रतिनिधि कए अपन पहल स स्थिति कए प्रबंधित करय पड़ैत अछि। न्यूपाने न॑ आरू कहलकै कि कुछ मामला म॑ एनआरएनए के प्रतिनिधि खुद परेशान मजदूरऽ क॑ समायोजित करै के कोशिश करतें हुअ॑ कानूनी मुद्दा आरू जेल तक के सामना करना पड़ै छै ।

ओ सरकार क ध्यान एहि दिस आकर्षित केलथि जे सालों स ‘शेल्टर हाउस’ क मांग क बावजूद सरकार एहि पर कोनो ध्यान नहि देलक अछि।

न्यौपाने नेपाली मजदूर के कौशल प्रशिक्षण देला के बाद ही विदेशी रोजगार के लेल भेजय के जरूरत पर सेहो जोर देलखिन्ह. एकरा लेली हुनी सरकार आरू एनआरएनए के सहयोग स॑ ‘स्किल अकादमी’ आरू स्किल टेस्टिंग सेंटर के स्थापना के सुझाव देलकै ।

ओ कहलनि जे, विदेश मे समस्या के सामना करय वाला नेपाली मजदूर के एनआरएनए के प्रतिनिधि तत्काल सहायता दैत छथि, मुदा औपचारिक कानूनी मान्यता के अभाव मे मुद्दा उठैत अछि। ओ सरकार स आग्रह केलथि जे एनआरएनए प्रतिनिधि कए ‘मानद’ या अवैतनिक श्रम दूत क रूप मे मान्यता देल जाए।

'एनआरएनए राजदूत जकाँ काज क' रहल अछि'।

संसद सदस्य तथा पूर्व संचारमन्त्री जगदीश खरेल विदेशमे रहल एनआरएनएस नेपालीके समस्याके समाधानमे राजदूतके रुपमे कार्यरत बतौलनि ।

अवैतनिक दूत के पद भले छोट बुझाइत हो मुदा नेपाली मजदूर के समस्या के समाधान में एकर महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका भ सकैत अछि से कहैत आवश्यक मामला पर सरकार के संग वकालत करबाक वचन देलनि।

'विदेश मे एनआरएन राजदूत जकाँ काज क' रहल छथि।' भले ही अवैतनिक दूत केरऽ पद छोटऽ लगै छै, लेकिन एकरऽ भूमिका महत्वपूर्ण छै । हम सरकार के संग जरूरी मामला पर पैरवी करय लेल प्रतिबद्ध छी।'

खरेल विदेश मे रहय वाला नेपाली के समस्या के सरकार आ राष्ट्रीय स्वतंत्र पार्टी बारीकी सं बुझि रहल अछि आ ओकर समाधान के दिशा मे काज करत से उल्लेख केलनि। विदेशी रोजगार के लेल जाय वाला मजदूर के कौशल विकास के लेल सब पक्ष के बीच सहयोग जरूरी सेहो कहलनि।

अकुशल मजदूर पठेबाक स्थिति समाप्त हेबाक चाही

संसद सदस्य ऐन महर के कहनाय छनि जे विदेशी रोजगार के व्यवस्थित, सुरक्षित, आ गरिमामय बनाबय पड़त. नेपाल केवल अकुशल मजदूर भेजय वाला देश के रूप मे जानल जाय वाला स्थिति के समाप्त करय लेल कौशल विकास पर विशेष ध्यान देल जाय पर जोर देलखिन्ह.

'विदेशी रोजगार के व्यवस्थित आ गरिमामय बनाबय पड़त।' कौशल विकास पर काज करय पड़त। नेपाल क॑ अकुशल मजदूर भेजै वाला देश के रूप म॑ ही जानलऽ जाय के स्थिति स॑ ऊपर उठना जरूरी छै,’ महर न॑ कहलकै ।

'दूतावास के बाद नेपाली एनआरएनए याद कर'।

विदेश मन्त्रालयके प्रवासी समन्वय प्रभागके उपप्रमुख कृशु क्षेत्री विदेशमे नेपाली दूतावास आ मिशनके बाद नेपालीके एनआरएनएके याद आबै छै ।

हुनी एनआरएनए के भूमिका के प्रशंसा करतें हुअय कहलकै कि बिना औपचारिक सरकारी मान्यता के भी एनआरएनए के प्रतिनिधि व्यावहारिक रूप स॑ श्रम दूत के रूप म॑ काम करी रहलऽ छै ।

'नेपाली दूतावास आ विदेश मे मिशन के बाद नेपाली के एनआरएनए याद करैत अछि।' बिना औपचारिक सरकारी मान्यता के सेहो एनआरएनएस मजदूर दूत के रूप मे काज क रहल अछि. ई भूमिका सराहनीय अछि,' क्षेत्री कहलनि ।

नेपाल मे विदेशी रोजगार पर अलग सम्मेलन होबय बला

एनआरएनए के अध्यक्ष डॉ. हेमराज शर्मा न॑ कहलकै कि विदेशी रोजगार के क्षेत्र म॑ आरू काम करै के जरूरत छै, आरू यही वजह स॑ ई विषय प॑ व्यापक चर्चा जरूरी छै । ओ जानकारी देलनि जे किछु मासक भीतर नेपाल मे विदेशी रोजगार पर अलग, पैघ सम्मेलन के आयोजन होयत।

'विदेशी रोजगारक क्षेत्र मे आओर काज करबाक आवश्यकता अछि।' एहि विषय पर व्यापक चर्चा आवश्यक हेबाक कारणे किछु मासक भीतर नेपाल मे अलग सम्मेलनक आयोजन करब,’ शर्मा कहलनि ।

ओ कहलनि जे, एनआरएनए विदेशी रोजगार के क्षेत्र मे बहुत काज क रहल अछि आ भविष्य मे आओर कार्यक्रम चलाओत।

विदेशी रोजगार मे मानसिक स्वास्थ्य के मुद्दा सेहो उठल

एनआरएनए के उपाध्यक्ष जूनू गुरुङ विदेशी रोजगार मे नेपाली के मानसिक स्वास्थ्य के संबंध मे भ रहल काज आ भविष्य मे होबय वाला कार्यक्रम के बारे मे जानकारी देलखिन्ह.

हुनी कहलकै कि विदेशी रोजगार के दौरान देखलौ जाय वाला मानसिक स्वास्थ्य संबंधी मुद्दा के पहचान करै आरू ओकरा संबोधित करै लेली आरू कार्यक्रम के जरूरत छै ।

सम्मेलन मे सरकार स आग्रह कैल गेल अछि जे विदेशी रोजगार मे अकुशल मजदूर नहि बल्कि कुशल जनशक्ति सेहो पठेबा लेल कौशल सिखाबय लेल प्रशिक्षण केंद्र आ कौशल परीक्षण केंद्र क स्थापना कैल जाए।

प्रतिभागी सब न॑ कहलकै कि कुशल जनशक्ति पैदा करै आरू विदेशी रोजगार म॑ ओकरऽ तैनाती के प्रबंधन लेली सरकार, निजी क्षेत्र, आरू एनआरएनए के बीच सहयोग जरूरी छै ।

कानूनी अधिकार के मांग

विभिन्न देशऽ के एनआरएनए प्रतिनिधि न॑ कहलकै कि भले ही परेशानी म॑ पड़लऽ नेपाली सिनी क॑ तत्काल बचाव, कानूनी, आरू अन्य सहायता दै छै, लेकिन औपचारिक कानूनी अधिकार के अभाव म॑ समस्या पैदा होय छै ।

हालांकि एनआरएनए अपन प्रतिनिधि कए अवैतनिक मजदूर दूत क रूप मे मान्यता देबा लेल नेपाल सरकार क ध्यान आकर्षित करैत आबि रहल अछि, मुदा एहि मुद्दा कए लागू नहि हेबाक कारण स सम्मेलन मे फेर स इ मुद्दा उठल।

कार्यक्रम के दौरान विभिन्न देश के नेपाली मजदूर के हालत, हुनका सब के सामने आबय वाला समस्या, आ समाधान पर विषयगत प्रस्तुति देल गेल।

दीपक पुन दक्षिण कोरिया मे नेपाली मजदूर, लाओस मे एकनाथ खतिवाडा, जापान मे खगराज गौतम, मलेशिया मे तिल्लोचन गौतम, आ मकाऊ मे युवराज नेउपाने के हालत पर प्रस्तुत केलनि। पत्रकार अनिल अधिकारी सेहो मजदूर के लेल समस्या आ समाधान पर प्रस्तुति देलखिन्ह.

एनआरएनए के मुख्य कार्यकारी अधिकारी राजेन्द्र कुमार राउत विदेशी रोजगार आ श्रम के क्षेत्र मे संस्था द्वारा कयल जा रहल काज के बारे मे जानकारी देलनि।

कार्यक्रम के संचालन यज्ञराज सुबेदी केने छलाह, आ मुख्य भाषण के लेल पत्रकार उद्धव भट्टराई नोट केने छलाह ।

एनआरएनए किछु समय बाद नेपाल मे विदेशी रोजगार पर अलग, पैघ पैमाना पर सम्मेलन के आयोजन करबाक घोषणा केलक अछि। एनआरएनए न॑ कहलकै कि सम्मेलन म॑ आरू सरकार, संबंधित निकाय, आरू प्रवासी नेपाली सिनी के बीच सुरक्षित विदेशी रोजगार, कौशल विकास, श्रम अधिकार, बचाव, आरू पुनर्वास जैसनऽ मुद्दा प॑ चर्चा करलऽ जैतै ।

full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug. 16: The government is planning to carry out a geological study of the landslide-affected areas of the western region of the country.

A meeting of the Monsoon Response Command Post of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) held Sunday decided to conduct a preliminary geological study of the landslide-hit areas at Thawang and Sunchhahari rural municipalities in Rolpa, Triveni municipality in Bajura and Bheri municipality in Jajarkot district.

The command post has also decided to deploy a study team in the field within three days under the leadership of NDRRMA, including representatives from the concerned agencies. The team will have the participation from the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology.

Likewise, the Monsoon Response Command Post has directed the concerned agencies to effectively advance the search, rescue, relief and rehabilitation works as the monsoon-induced disasters have caused havoc in different districts, according to the NDRRMA.

The NDRRMA has expressed its serious concern to the loss caused due to the landslides in some districts, and has urged to immediately expedite the rescue and relief operations targeting the affected households.

Today's meeting of the command post has asked the concerned district administration offices, district disaster management committee and local levels to ensure treatment to the injured ones for free and provide relief materials to the affected households based on a rapid assessment of the disasters.

Similarly, the NDRRMA has directed for the construction of temporary housing for those affected from the disasters and initiate processes for retrofitting of the private houses and provide grant for the reconstruction and rehabilitation at the earliest possible time.

The NDRRMA has also urged the people to exercise high alertness during the monsoon season as the risk of landslide has increased due to torrential rain in the hilly and mountainous regions in the country.

Furthermore, the local residents have been advised to avoid non-essential travel as the risks of inundation, flooding, flash flood and debris flows remain high in different parts of the country. (RSS)

title: Deuba faction’s Hindu line opens new fault line in Nepali Congress - The Kathmandu Post
description: Deuba faction’s Hindu line opens new fault line in Nepali Congress  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
“I am a Hindu, I am a Hindu, I am a Hindu.”

Former prime minister Sher Bahadur Deuba, who returned to Nepal last Thursday after spending nearly five months abroad, made the emphatic statement at the closing ceremony of a three-day national gathering organised by a faction of the Nepali Congress in Sukedhara on Sunday.

He further said that his personal faith did not mean he opposed other religions or rejected Nepal’s religious freedom.

“And I have love and reverence for Buddha and Buddhism. The world today recognises Buddhism. Today, Buddhism is also referred to as a scientific religion and is regarded as such. Likewise, ours is a country that respects nature-based religions. The Rai and Limbu communities follow nature-based religions, and we must respect all of them. I respect them.”

The Deuba faction’s decision to promote Sanatan religion as a national identity has opened a new ideological fault line in the Nepali Congress, while its rejection of Gagan Thapa’s leadership threatens to deepen the party’s organisational dispute.

The three-day gathering concluded on Sunday with a five-point declaration that commits the party to promoting Sanatan religion as a national identity while pledging to protect Hindu, Buddhist, Kirat and nature-based faiths and the religious freedom of all communities.

But the religious provision was added at the last minute and was absent from the 20-point conclusion prepared for the gathering, according to Congress leaders.

The earlier document described Nepal as a multi-ethnic, multilingual, multi-religious and multicultural country and guaranteed communities the freedom to practise and preserve their faiths and cultures.

Bimalendra Nidhi’s political proposal also made no mention of promoting Sanatan religion as a national identity or supporting a Hindu state. The gathering was initially expected to endorse the 20-point conclusion.

After Deuba reviewed the proposal, however, a separate five-point declaration was prepared under his direction, a Congress leader said. It recognised Nepal’s traditional religious and cultural heritage as part of its national identity and committed the party to promoting Sanatan religion while protecting Hindu, Buddhist, Kirat and nature-based faiths and religious freedom.

The move faced resistance within the Deuba camp. Nidhi objected to the new declaration, which was absent from his proposal, and exchanged words with Prakash Sharan Mahat on the stage, according to Congress leaders. The five-point declaration was nevertheless read out and endorsed by the gathering.

Political analysts say the move marks a departure from the party’s position since the 2015 Constitution, which defines Nepal as a secular state. They see it as an attempt to establish a distinct political identity after losing control to Thapa.

“The decision to adopt the Hindu line may have been driven by Deuba’s search for political and personal security,” said Krishna Khanal, a political analyst. “Otherwise, religion—whether Hinduism or secularism—does not appear to have been an issue that mattered much to him as a leader.”

Khanal said Deuba’s decision should not necessarily be read as the result of a long-developed political philosophy. “There may have been an influence of Hindu extremists in India,” he said. “The thinking could be that taking this line would make politics and security easier. I do not see it coming from a long-term ideological view of Nepal. Personally, I do not think Deuba makes much distinction between secularism and Hinduism.”

The issue has been present in Congress for years. At the party’s Mahasamiti meeting in February 2024, more than 1,000 members signed a petition calling for Nepal to be restored as a Hindu state. The campaign was led by lawmaker Shankar Bhandari, but Deuba, who was party president at the time, did not formally endorse the demand.

This time, the Deuba camp has gone further by formally adopting Sanatan religion as a national identity. The declaration says Nepal’s longstanding religious and cultural traditions are part of its national identity and commits the party to preserving Hindu, Buddhist, Kirat and nature-based religions while ensuring religious freedom, tolerance and social harmony.

Congress leader Prakash Sharan Mahat described the decision as an important departure in the party’s internal politics after the constitution was promulgated. He said support for a Hindu state had existed in Congress forums before, but the party leadership had not formally taken ownership of it.

“Until now, Congress had repeatedly said that secularism was a provision of the constitution,” said Mahat. “This time, we have said that Sanatan religion is a national identity and have adopted this as a policy through the gathering.”

He said the gathering also rejected the social democratic policy advanced by Thapa after the special general convention and returned to BP Koirala’s concept of democratic socialism. “There are two important departures,” said Mahat. “One is the return to democratic socialism, and the other, more important one, is the position on Hindu religion.”

The decision was not without opposition inside the Deuba camp. According to Congress leaders, Nidhi tried to stop the religious provision from being inserted into the declaration because it was absent from the political proposal presented to the gathering. Another senior leader, Krishna Prasad Sitaula, also expressed dissatisfaction.

Nidhi has consistently defended republicanism, federalism and secularism as achievements of the constitution. Sitaula was coordinator of the constitution drafting committee during the constitution-making process. One Congress leader said Bhandari, who has long advocated a Hindu state and constitutional monarchy, was prevented from speaking at the opening session to avoid creating a Hindu-state atmosphere.

The organisational dispute is even more consequential. The Deuba faction has rejected the special general convention held in January and the central committee elected under Thapa. It has declared that the 15th general convention should be organised by the central committee elected through the 14th general convention and held under Deuba’s leadership.

The position directly challenges the Election Commission’s recognition of the Thapa-led Congress in January. The commission had ruled that the special convention was valid because the party statute allows at least 40 percent of general convention representatives to demand such a gathering. It also held that general convention representatives are the party’s supreme authority.

The Supreme Court in April upheld the recognition of the Thapa-led faction, ending the immediate legitimacy dispute. But the Deuba faction filed a review petition in July, bringing the dispute back before the court.

This legal battle has become intertwined with the party’s preparations for its next regular general convention. Congress Vice-President Bishwa Prakash Sharma has argued that rejecting the leadership recognised by both the Election Commission and the Supreme Court risks further dividing the party.

“A decision made at a programme attended by Deuba himself amounts to contempt of court,” said Sharma. “The court’s decision to grant permission for review did not make Deuba the party president. Going beyond what the court has said and calling him president is contempt.”

The Deuba faction, however, argues that Congress should not proceed with organisational activities while the leadership dispute remains before the Supreme Court. NP Saud said holding a general convention while the review petition is pending could affect the final outcome of the case and amount to contempt of court.

“If the party continues towards the convention by ignoring the Supreme Court’s order on the review, that would amount to contempt,” said Saud. “No action should be taken that could adversely affect the pending case related to the Congress dispute.”

The Thapa camp has taken the opposite view, saying the party cannot indefinitely delay its regular convention because of the court case. Sharma said the existing schedule for the central convention should remain in place, although lower-level schedules could be adjusted by the central committee.

The dispute comes after a dramatic year for Congress. Thapa and Sharma called the special general convention after more than half of the elected representatives demanded it. The Deuba camp boycotted the gathering, but the convention elected Thapa president and a new central committee. The Election Commission then recognised the new leadership.

The party’s crisis has also been worsened by its poor performance in the March elections. Congress won only 38 seats, down sharply from the 89 seats it had secured in the 2022 election. Thapa later resigned as party president, taking responsibility for the electoral defeat, but the central committee rejected his resignation.

The latest Hindu identity decision therefore comes at a particularly unsettled moment. For Deuba’s supporters, it offers a way to preserve their political space and appeal to traditional voters. For critics, it risks weakening Congress’s commitment to the constitutional order and widening the ideological gap with Thapa’s reform-oriented camp.

“While the party’s decisions are under discussion, it is not appropriate to comment on such matters,” Sharma said. “But anything adopted by the gathering that strengthens the organisation and serves Congress, democracy and the country will not be viewed negatively. We will discuss how such matters can be incorporated.”

NEW DELHI: Army chief General Dhiraj Seth has embarked on a visit to Nepal from August 17 to 19 to strengthen defence cooperation and military-to-military ties between the two neighbouring countries.On Monday, Gen Seth will interact with the Chief of the Army Staff, Nepali Army and will be briefed by the Director General Military Operations, Nepali Army, on issues of mutual interest before laying a wreath at Army Pavilion, Tundikhel and receiving a guard of honour at the Nepali Army Headquarters. The visit underscores the deep-rooted historical, cultural and military ties between India and Nepal and will provide an opportunity to explore new avenues of cooperation between the two armies.General Dhiraj Seth will also attend the investiture ceremony at Nepal’s Rashtrapati Bhawan, where, in keeping with the unique tradition between the Indian and Nepali Armies, he will be conferred the Honorary Rank of General of the Nepali Army by Nepal President Ram Chandra Paudel.On Tuesday, the Army chief will address the student officers of the Army Command and Staff Course at Shivapuri and interact with instructors and foreign student officers.He will also be interacting with senior dignitaries of Nepal on issues of mutual interest.On Wednesday, General Dhiraj Seth will attend an ex-servicemen rally at Pokhara, felicitate Veer Naris and gallantry awardees and interact with Indian Army veterans.India and Nepal are two nations with shared historical, social and cultural linkages which remain unparalleled in the world. Terms fondly referred to as the ‘Roti Beti Ka Rishta’, the Janakpur-Ayodhya and the Lumbini-Bodhgaya connect make both nations natural partners with symbiotic relations.

जनरल धीरज सेठ नेपाल के राष्ट्रपति भवन में इन्वेस्टिच्यूशन समारोह में सेहो भाग लेताह, जतय हुनका नेपाल के राष्ट्रपति रामचंद्र पौडेल द्वारा नेपाली सेना के जनरल के मानद पद स सम्मानित कायल जायत।

नई दिल्ली, मिथिला मिरर: सेना प्रमुख जनरल धीरज सेठ दुनू पड़ोसी देशक बीच रक्षा सहयोग आ सैन्य-सैन्य संबंध केँ मजबूत करबाक लेल 17 सँ 19 अगस्त धरि नेपाल यात्रा पर निकलल छथि।सोमदिन जनरल सेठ नेपाली सेनाक सेना प्रमुखक संग बातचीत करताह आ नेपाली सेनाक महानिदेशक सैन्य अभियान द्वारा आपसी मुद्दा पर अवगत कराओल जेताह सेना मंडप, टुंडीखेल मे माल्यार्पण आ नेपाली सेना मुख्यालय मे गार्ड ऑफ ऑनर प्राप्त करबा स पहिने ब्याज। ई यात्रा भारत आरू नेपाल के बीच गहरी जड़ वाला ऐतिहासिक, सांस्कृतिक आरू सैन्य संबंध के रेखांकित करै छै आरू ई दूनू सेना के बीच सहयोग के नया रास्ता खोजै के अवसर प्रदान करतै ।नेपाल के राष्ट्रपति भवन मँ इन्वेस्टिच्यूशन समारोह मँ जनरल धीरज सेठ भी शामिल होतै, जहां भारतीय आरू नेपाली सेना के बीच के विशिष्ट परंपरा के अनुरूप हुनका जनरल ऑफ द के मानद पद स॑ सम्मानित करलऽ जैतै नेपालक राष्ट्रपति रामचन्द्र पौडेल द्वारा नेपाली सेना।मंगलदिन सेना प्रमुख शिवपुरीमे सेना कमान आ कर्मचारी पाठ्यक्रमक छात्र अधिकारी सभकेँ संबोधित करताह आ प्रशिक्षक आ विदेशी छात्र अधिकारी सभसँ बातचीत करताह।ओ नेपालक वरिष्ठ गणमान्य लोकनिसँ सेहो आपसी हितक विषयमे बातचीत करताह।बुधदिन जनरल धीरज सेठ पूर्व सैनिकक रैलीमे भाग लेताह पोखरा, वीर नारिस आ बहादुरी से सम्मानित के सम्मानित करै छै आरू भारतीय सेना के दिग्गज सिनी के साथ बातचीत करै छै।भारत आरू नेपाल साझा ऐतिहासिक, सामाजिक आरू सांस्कृतिक संबंध वाला दू राष्ट्र छै जे दुनिया में बेजोड़ छै। ‘रोटी बेटी का रिश्ता’, जनकपुर-अयोध्या आरू लुम्बिनी-बोधगया कनेक्ट के नाम स॑ प्रेम स॑ संदर्भित शब्द दूनू राष्ट्र क॑ सहजीवी संबंध के साथ प्राकृतिक भागीदार बनाबै छै ।
